detailed_description: The CSP Generator builds a `Content-Security-Policy` string from a fixed list of directives in the browser. Each directive has an enable checkbox, the values you have added so far as removable chips, and a small dropdown of common keywords (such as `'self'`, `'none'`, `'unsafe-inline'`, `https:`, `data:`) for adding new values. You can reset to the default directive list, switch the output between an HTTP header line and a `<meta http-equiv>` tag, and copy the result. The tool does not validate nonces, hashes, or URLs against any CSP level, warn about deprecated keywords, support `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` mode, accept free-form custom values outside the dropdown, or test the generated policy against a real page.
usage_steps: Toggle the enable checkbox on each directive you want to include in the policy.
Use the per-directive dropdown to add common values, and remove existing chips with the × button.
Switch the output format between HTTP header and meta tag using the dropdown above the result panel.
Review the generated `Content-Security-Policy` line in the output area.
Click Copy to put the result on your clipboard, or Reset Defaults to restore the starting directive set.
usage_examples: Draft a starter `script-src 'self'` and `style-src 'self'` policy for a small static site.
Add `data:` and `https:` to `img-src` for a page that loads images from CDNs and inline data URIs.
Switch the output to a meta tag to embed a basic policy directly in an HTML document for testing.
Reset the directives and rebuild a minimal policy when you want to start from a clean baseline.
